text:
Matt Boldy scored three goals in Toronto, and the Maple Leafs are now winless in five (0-5-0). His hat trick, the first of which came with 7 seconds left in the first period's final stretch, a snap shot at 17:53, turned a tied game in the second period into a 5-2 Minnesota win. Drafted 12th overall by the Wild in 2019 and a Boston College product, Boldy took a power-play slap shot at 9:55 of the second to tie it, then added the go-ahead goal early in the third. Kirill Kaprizov, a 135th overall pick in 2015, assisted on three of Minnesota's goals.

Toronto did not play badly. The Leafs had 66 shot attempts to Minnesota's 58 and took the lead on Zack MacEwen's goal at 6:59 of the second, two and a half minutes after Auston Matthews tied it. But the quality of chances was close: we have Minnesota at 2.96 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) to Toronto's 2.45, which works out to a 56 to 44 split in how often each side would win if the game were replayed. Minnesota's third goal came on a chance worth just 8%, and Danila Yurov's empty-net-era insurance goal late in the third was a 5% look. Anthony Stolarz allowed 1.2 goals more than the shots he faced deserved, while Jesper Wallstedt stopped 26 of 28.

Minnesota leaves with a road win built on finishing. Toronto sits winless in five and still looking for the stretch of goaltending and finishing that would match how often it controls the puck.
